title: Applied Anomalies I: Reading Unstable Systems
description: Internal seminar on identifying, logging and characterising acoustic and computational edge cases. Covers feedback onset, hysteresis loops, boundary instability and the discipline of writing an anomaly note that someone else can act on.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of signal flow and gain staging
Familiarity with the ZIAA research-note format
teaches: Recognising the onset conditions of electroacoustic feedback
Characterising hysteresis as a measurable, repeatable parameter
Writing an actionable anomaly research note with telemetry attached
assesses: Anomaly characterisation exercise on bench hardware
Written research note to archive standard

syllabusSections.name: What counts as an anomaly
syllabusSections.description: Distinguishing edge-case behaviour from ordinary fault, and why the Institute treats the former as material.

syllabusSections.name: Onset conditions
syllabusSections.description: Gain structure, delay, room coupling and the geometry of feedback onset.

syllabusSections.name: Hysteresis measurement
syllabusSections.description: Sweeping a system up and down to separate reversible from irreversible behaviour.

syllabusSections.name: Writing it down
syllabusSections.description: Telemetry, reproducibility and the archive's research-note standard.

title: Autonomous Agents & Procedural Scoring
description: Builds generative systems that make musical decisions in real time, and confronts the evaluation problem: how to tell whether an agent's output is interesting, merely novel, or noise.
prerequisites: Comfort with a scripting language for audio
teaches: Designing decision loops that stay musically legible over long time spans
Implementing procedural scoring under real-time constraints
Constructing an evaluation protocol for generative output
assesses: A live agent performing for twenty minutes without operator intervention

syllabusSections.name: Agency and legibility
syllabusSections.description: What makes a generative system read as intentional rather than random.

syllabusSections.name: Decision architectures
syllabusSections.description: Markov processes, constraint grammars, learned policies.

syllabusSections.name: Real-time discipline
syllabusSections.description: Budgeting CPU, avoiding allocation in the audio path, deterministic scheduling.

syllabusSections.name: Evaluation
syllabusSections.description: Protocols for judging output, including the negative-result case.

title: Real-Time DSP in the Browser
description: The Institute's core software seminar. AudioWorklet processors, buffer discipline, latency budgeting and WebAssembly DSP cores, taught against the code that runs the public browser instruments.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of sampling and filters
teaches: Writing an AudioWorklet processor that never allocates on the audio thread
Budgeting and measuring end-to-end latency
Calling a WebAssembly DSP core from a worklet without copying
assesses: A working browser instrument passing the Institute's latency and dropout budget
Code review against the archive's software standard

syllabusSections.name: The audio graph
syllabusSections.description: Nodes, rendering quanta and what actually happens per block.

syllabusSections.name: Worklet discipline
syllabusSections.description: Allocation, locking and the cost of a single branch in the render path.

syllabusSections.name: Latency accounting
syllabusSections.description: Input-to-output measurement, base latency, output compensation.

syllabusSections.name: WebAssembly cores
syllabusSections.description: Shared buffers, SIMD and avoiding the copy.

title: Signal Archaeology: Recovering Unplayable Media
description: Hands-on recovery practice: optical scanning of groove geometry, magnetic remanence readout, and the reconstruction pipelines that turn a scan into listenable audio — with the ethics of intervening in a damaged original.
prerequisites: Prior contact with archival media handling
teaches: Choosing a non-destructive readout method for a given carrier
Optical scan capture and groove-geometry reconstruction
Documenting intervention so a recovery remains auditable
assesses: Recovery of a provided damaged carrier to a documented, reproducible result

syllabusSections.name: Carrier triage
syllabusSections.description: Assessing lacquer, wax, shellac and magnetic carriers before any contact.

syllabusSections.name: Optical extraction
syllabusSections.description: Scanning geometry, registration and depth recovery.

syllabusSections.name: Magnetic readout
syllabusSections.description: Remanence imaging and transport-free reconstruction.

syllabusSections.name: Provenance and audit
syllabusSections.description: Recording every intervention so the recovery can be reviewed.

instances.facility: Studio C (Signal Archaeology & Archival Audio Lab)

title: Physical Interfaces: Haptics, Floors & Microtonal Surfaces
description: Fabrication and calibration of performance surfaces, from transducer-driven tactile panels to motorised haptic controllers, with the metrology needed to make a surface repeatable enough to perform on.
teaches: Coupling transducers to a surface without destroying its acoustic identity
Calibrating a motorised controller to sub-millimetre repeatability
Designing microtonal layout for a player who cannot see the fretboard
assesses: A fabricated surface meeting the Institute's repeatability tolerance

syllabusSections.name: Surface acoustics
syllabusSections.description: What a panel does to a transducer, and vice versa.

syllabusSections.name: Actuation
syllabusSections.description: Solenoids, motors and the mechanics of controllable force.

syllabusSections.name: Metrology
syllabusSections.description: Measuring repeatability, backlash and drift.

syllabusSections.name: Playability
syllabusSections.description: Layout, feedback and the performer's mental model.

title: Bench Practice: Analog Signal Paths & Resonant Materials
description: Foundational bench seminar on discrete analog signal paths and the acoustic behaviour of resonant materials — resonant woods, mineral lithophones and contact transduction.
prerequisites: None; safety briefing delivered in the first session
teaches: Building and debugging a discrete analog signal path
Measuring the resonant behaviour of a material sample
Mounting and matching contact transducers
assesses: A working bench signal path with a documented noise floor

syllabusSections.name: Signal path basics
syllabusSections.description: Gain stages, impedance and where noise actually comes from.

syllabusSections.name: Material resonance
syllabusSections.description: Modes, damping and why wood and stone disagree.

syllabusSections.name: Contact transduction
syllabusSections.description: Coupling, mounting pressure and matching.

syllabusSections.name: Documentation
syllabusSections.description: Bill of materials, tolerance and the archive record.

title: Spatial Systems: Ambisonics & Loudspeaker Geometry
description: High-order ambisonics, decoder design for non-ideal rooms, and the compositional consequences of committing to a fixed three-dimensional loudspeaker geometry.
teaches: Choosing an ambisonic order for a given room and array
Designing and measuring a decoder for a non-ideal space
Composing for a fixed geometry without treating it as a limitation
assesses: A measured decoder for the Institute's dome, with a listening report

syllabusSections.name: Spherical harmonics in practice
syllabusSections.description: Orders, truncation and what you lose at each step.

syllabusSections.name: Decoder design
syllabusSections.description: All-round, in-phase and the trade-offs nobody advertises.

syllabusSections.name: Room interaction
syllabusSections.description: Reflections, modes and why the room is part of the decoder.

syllabusSections.name: Composing the array
syllabusSections.description: Writing for a fixed geometry as a compositional resource.

title: Speculative Engineering & the Design-Fiction Disclosure
description: How to write a design-fiction disclosure that is rigorous enough to be useful and clearly enough framed not to be mistaken for a legal filing. Claim structure, prior-art critique and the register of patent literature.
teaches: Structuring an independent claim and its dependent tree
Writing a prior-art critique that is honest about what exists
Framing speculative work so it cannot be mistaken for a legal instrument
assesses: One complete speculative patent dossier passing the Institute's disclosure review

syllabusSections.name: The register
syllabusSections.description: How patent literature reads, and what to borrow from it.

syllabusSections.name: Claims
syllabusSections.description: Independent and dependent structure, scope and the over-claiming trap.

syllabusSections.name: Prior art
syllabusSections.description: Researching honestly and writing critique that holds up.

syllabusSections.name: Disclosure ethics
syllabusSections.description: Keeping design fiction visibly separate from legal filing.

title: Remote Station Deployment & Unattended Listening
description: Field practice for the listening estate: site survey, hydrophone and infrasound installation, power plant sizing, environmental hardening, and designing a station to survive a year without a visit.
prerequisites: Field safety certification delivered on site
teaches: Surveying a site for acoustic and electromagnetic noise before installing
Sizing power and storage for a year of unattended operation
Designing telemetry and failure reporting for a station nobody can reach
assesses: A deployment plan and power budget for a nominated site

syllabusSections.name: Site survey
syllabusSections.description: Noise floors, access, and the constraints that decide everything else.

syllabusSections.name: Sensor installation
syllabusSections.description: Hydrophones, infrasound lines and grounding.

syllabusSections.name: Power and survival
syllabusSections.description: Solar, battery, thermal design and the winter margin.

syllabusSections.name: Telemetry
syllabusSections.description: Backhaul, watchdogs and knowing a station is dying from far away.

title: Listening Practice & Soundscape Field Method
description: Training in disciplined listening: soundscape walks, baselining anthropogenic noise, and the note-taking method that turns subjective listening into data another researcher can compare against.
teaches: Conducting a repeatable soundscape walk
Baselining anthropogenic noise at a site
Writing listening notes that are comparable across observers
assesses: A documented soundscape walk with baseline measurements

syllabusSections.name: Disciplined listening
syllabusSections.description: Attention, expectation and the observer effect.

syllabusSections.name: Baselining
syllabusSections.description: What to measure, for how long, and when.

syllabusSections.name: Notation
syllabusSections.description: Making subjective listening comparable.

syllabusSections.name: Ecology
syllabusSections.description: Bioacoustic markers and what they indicate.
